answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the velvet registry records each claim and the ledge audit publishes every slash. A farm must therefore either lie, which the meadow graph proves on replay, or recruit 199 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 34% of the attester's bond. That is 12 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
